speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a chronic wound on your right lower leg; to begin our assessment, how long have you had this wound, and what does it look like on the surface?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of a DVT five years ago combined with chronic swelling and a family history strongly suggests a venous etiology, but given the six-month duration, I need to rule out an underlying malignancy. Has the wound ever bled spontaneously or changed appearance rapidly? REQUEST IMAGES: Lower_leg_wound_close_up.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer secondary to chronic venous insufficiency.
